newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end higher, bullish on re-election.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end higher, bullish on re-election.

text.p: Brazil shares closed up 1.93 percent on heavy buying supported by investor optimism that Congress will approve an amendment allowing presidential re-election by mid-January, brokers said.
"The market is optimistic that Congress will approve the amendment allowing presidential re-election," said Andre Pereira, a broker at a Sao Paulo brokerage house.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most-active shares rose 1,380 points to close at 72,975 points. Turnover was heavy at 752 million reais ($723.1 million).
A lower house committee is slated to vote on the re-election issue on January 13. Those will be followed by two votes in the Chamber of Deputies on January 15 and 22.
Today's trading was also boosted by expectations that the government will exempt stock trade from the new CPMF tax.
"I think the government will not adopt any retaliation against foreign investors because it needs them in the privatization," Pereira said.
Today's big winners included state-controlled power firms. Minas Gerais Cemig preferred stock jumped 7.75 percent to close at 38.80 reais.

Sao Paulo state power firms CPFL and Cesp preferred stock rose 5.71 percent to 111 reais, and 4.77 percent to 45 reais, respectively. Both firms benefitted from news that consulting firms would begin bidding for contracts to advise on the sale of Sao Paulo state power firms this week.
The strong performance of power firms pushed up the bolsa's Electrical Energy Index .IEE of the nine most liquid power shares, which rose 3.26 percent to end at 2,064 points.

Blue chip gainers included Telebras preferred, which rose 2.04 percent to end at 82.60 reais. Mining giant Vale do Rio Doce preferred closed at 21.90 reais, up 5.29 percent. Petrobras preferred rose 2.85 percent to end at 180 reais.
Eletrobras ELE_p.SA preferred, however, dropped 1.5 percent to end at 393 reais as investors changed positions and moved into other power firms, brokers said.
The market's wider Brazil index (IBX) of 100 leading shares also rose, climbing 2.37 percent to close at 1,597 points.
